title: Role of IFI204 in Modulating NF-KappaB Pathway and Myocardial Protection in Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
authors: Xing, Zhi; Abudureyimu, Shajidan; Abulaiti, Palida; Wang, Yu; Lyu, MaoLin; Gao, Ying
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过机器学习识别I/R损伤关键基因Ifi204并验证其经NF-κB通路调控心肌保护，但核心是心肌损伤机制而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，仅提及NF-κB信号通路，无TF-DNA结合或互作机制研究。
abstract: Ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury remains a major contributor to myocardial damage, significantly impacting cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This study identifies key genes and pathways involved in I/R-induced myocardial injury through differential gene expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Functional enrichment analyses, including Gene Ontology, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, and Disease Ontology, highlight the involvement of immune response and oxidative stress pathways in I/R injury. Machine learning approaches, such as LASSO, Support Vector Machine Recursive Feature Elimination, and Random Forest, were employed to identify feature genes predictive of I/R progression, with Ifi204 emerging as a critical factor. The role of interferon-induced protein 204 (Ifi204) in myocardial protection during I/R injury was further explored using a heart-specific Ifi204 knockout mouse model. The effects of Ifi204 deficiency on myocardial injury, inflammation, and oxidative stress were assessed. Notably, heart-specific Ifi204 knockout mice demonstrated reduced myocardial infarct size, improved heart function, and lower serum markers of myocardial injury, including creatine kinase, lactate dehydrogenase, and cardiac troponin T. These mice also exhibited attenuated oxidative stress and suppressed NF-kappaB signaling, as evidenced by reduced malondialdehyde levels and increased superoxide dismutase activity. Furthermore, overexpression of Ifi204 in primary cardiomyocytes enhanced the inflammatory response via NF-kappaB activation, leading to increased secretion of proinflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-alpha and IL-6. These effects were mitigated by NF-kappaB inhibition, suggesting that Ifi204 modulates inflammation through NF-kappaB signaling. This study provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying myocardial I/R injury and positions Ifi204 as a potential therapeutic target for cardiovascular diseases.
abstract_zh: 缺血再灌注（I/R）损伤仍是心肌损伤的主要诱因，显著影响心血管疾病的发病率和死亡率。本研究通过差异基因表达分析和加权基因共表达网络分析，鉴定了参与I/R诱导心肌损伤的关键基因和通路。功能富集分析，包括基因本体论（Gene Ontology）、京都基因与基因组百科全书（Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes）和疾病本体论（Disease Ontology），强调了免疫反应和氧化应激通路在I/R损伤中的作用。采用机器学习方法，如LASSO、支持向量机递归特征消除（Support Vector Machine Recursive Feature Elimination）和随机森林（Random Forest），以鉴定预测I/R进展的特征基因，其中Ifi204被确定为一个关键因子。进一步利用心脏特异性Ifi204敲除小鼠模型，探讨了干扰素诱导蛋白204（Ifi204）在I/R损伤期间心肌保护中的作用。评估了Ifi204缺失对心肌损伤、炎症和氧化应激的影响。值得注意的是，心脏特异性Ifi204敲除小鼠表现出心肌梗死面积减少、心脏功能改善以及血清心肌损伤标志物（包括肌酸激酶、乳酸脱氢酶和心肌肌钙蛋白T）水平降低。这些小鼠还表现出氧化应激减弱和NF-kappaB信号传导抑制，这通过丙二醛水平降低和超氧化物歧化酶活性增加得以证实。此外，在原代心肌细胞中过表达Ifi204通过NF-kappaB激活增强了炎症反应，导致促炎细胞因子（如TNF-alpha和IL-6）分泌增加。这些效应通过NF-kappaB抑制得到缓解，表明Ifi204通过NF-kappaB信号传导调节炎症。本研究为心肌I/R损伤的分子机制提供了新见解，并将Ifi204定位为心血管疾病的潜在治疗靶点。
